title: Your Life as a VC at Every Level (One Bet Pays For All)
hook: You get a vote on none of the three hundred pitch decks in your inbox this week — until the one deal you can't stop believing in either makes your career or ends it. Climb from unpaid opinions to a fund with your own name on the door, and find out what 'return the fund' really costs.
body: POV: you're a venture capitalist climbing from unpaid-opinion analyst to the general partner of your own fund, then to the pensions and endowments who decide which funds even get to exist. Real, verified mechanics woven in: the actual Correlation Ventures power-law data (roughly 65% of VC deals return less than the money put in; fewer than 4% return 10x or more, and that sliver produces most of the industry's returns) — the real math behind 'one bet pays for all.' Bessemer Venture Partners' real, public 'Anti-Portfolio' (founding partner David Cowan passing on meeting Larry Page and Sergey Brin in a garage, 1999-2000). Real 2025-2026 compensation and carry structures by level, real GP-commit norms (roughly 1.5-1.7% of the fund, personal money, locked up for a decade), and real January-2026 AUM figures for Andreessen Horowitz, Sequoia Capital, and the entire US and global venture industry. A dramatized cautionary POV — the fund, the founder, and the portfolio company are a fictional composite; the mechanics and numbers are real and sourced. Watch the whole series — every life, every level, every way the climb costs you. For educational and entertainment purposes.
pinned: The scariest real number in this episode isn't the size of any fund — it's the power law: Correlation Ventures found roughly 65% of VC deals return less than the money that went in, and fewer than 4% return 10x or more. Which level do you think ends the most careers: the board seat, or the mark-to-zero call?
poll: Which stage would break you first? LEVEL 03 (the board seat) / LEVEL 04 (the mark-to-zero call) / LEVEL 06 (raising your own Fund I) / LEVEL 08 (realizing you're not even 1% of the industry)
